newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech says profits rise 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech says profits rise 10 percent.

text.p: Ameritech Corp. said Tuesday its operating earnings jumped 10 percent in the latest quarter, as the Baby Bell reported strong gains in the cellular phone and paging businesses.

The company had operating profits of $624 million or $1.13 a share in the second quarter, up from year-earlier earnings of $567 million, or $1.02 a share. The results exclude a charge of $87 million to restructure the Belgian telecommunications company Belgacom, one of its overseas investments.
Revenues rose to $3.99 billion from $3.74 billion.
Ameritech said its cellular customers grew 31 percent to 2.9 million, paging customers were up 38 percent to 1.3 million and security monitoring customers rose 42 percent to 566,000.
Ameritech said it added 148,000 cellular customers during the quarter and 344,000 over the first six month -- the largest second-quarter and first-half gains in the company's history.

The Chicago-based company said it continued its push to enter the long-distance market in its five-state region. Ameritech has applied for approval to provide service in Michigan, and said the Federal Communications Commission is expected to rule on that application by Aug. 19.
"Ameritech plans to file for long distance entry in additional states in the near future," the company said in a statement.
Ameritech's stock was off $1 at $67.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
